lesson.title: What solid does this make?
lesson.subtitle: P4 nets revision
lesson.objective: Name a solid from its net and count its faces, edges and vertices.
lesson.story: A flat net will be folded up into a solid.

steps.title: Count the faces
steps.prompt: How many flat faces does the solid made by this net have?
hints: Each flat shape in the net becomes one face of the solid.
Count the shapes drawn, one by one.
Count every shape, triangles and rectangles alike.
The net has 6 shapes, so the solid has 6 faces. Enter 6.

steps.title: Name the solid
steps.prompt: Which solid does this net make when it is folded up?
hints: Look at the kinds of shapes in the net.
Count how many of each kind there are.
This net has 6 rectangles. Think about which solid has faces like that.
Choose the cuboid.

steps.title: Count the edges
steps.prompt: How many edges does the solid have? An edge is where two faces meet.
hints: Each shape in the net has sides. Every edge of the solid is made from two sides that fold together.
Count the sides of every shape and add them up.
The shapes have 24 sides in all. Two sides make one edge, so work out 24 ÷ 2.

steps.title: Count the vertices
steps.prompt: How many vertices does the solid have? A vertex is a corner where edges meet.
hints: Picture the folded solid and the corners you could point to.
Count the corners one at a time, so you do not count any twice.
A check: the number of faces plus the number of vertices is 2 more than the number of edges. You found 6 faces and 12 edges.
The solid has 8 vertices. Enter 8.

steps.title: Explain your thinking
steps.prompt: How does a net become a solid?

choices.label: Every net folds into a cube, whatever flat shapes it is made from.
The flat shapes become the faces and fold along the joined edges.
The flat shapes become the edges of the solid when the net is folded.

hints: Think about opening up a box and pressing it flat.
Each flat piece of the box was one side of it.
A net can make many different solids, not only a cube.
Choose the explanation about shapes becoming faces.
